title: The Vital Point
intro: You know that two eyes live. Now the part that is actually played: most groups have neither two eyes nor none, but a space that could become either.
Whoever plays first inside that space decides which. There is usually one point that decides it, and it is usually the middle.

steps.instruction: Black surrounds three points and has not divided them. You are White. Play the point that stops this group ever having two eyes.
steps.hint: The middle of the three. Not an end.
steps.explanation: Dead. Black cannot divide the space now, and cannot capture your stone without filling their own last liberties to do it. One move, played inside, and a group of twelve stones will never come back.

steps.instruction: The same position, and this time it is your move. Live.
steps.explanation: Two eyes, and alive for good. The point that kills and the point that lives are one point -- which is what a vital point is, and why the race for it is the whole of life and death.

steps.instruction: Two points this time. You are White again -- settle it.
steps.hint: Either point. There is no vital point here, because there is no room for one.
steps.explanation: A space of two can never become two eyes -- there is nowhere to put the dividing wall. This group was dead before you touched it, and Black playing first would not have helped either.

outro: Two points is dead. Three lives only for whoever plays the middle first. Four in a row is already alive and needs nothing from you.
Do not memorise that. Ask, every time, whether the space can still be cut into two -- and if it can, notice that it is somebody's move.
